correctness.rationale: Exact proof: avoidance is a downward weak-order ideal; Stembridge establishes distributivity of each principal weak-order interval. The resulting global join-irreducible coordinate sets change one coordinate on each cover and give the exact meet-rank graph metric. The 321 condition partitions permutations into two increasing subsequences, giving inversion bound floor(n^2/4), with all equality cases uniquely two-block. Explicit two-block pairs have disjoint simple atom sets and hence identity meet, attain 2M for odd n and 2M-1 for even n; uniqueness of the even maximum proves the upper bound. Full adjacency-graph BFS compares every state-pair distance for n=1,...,8 to independent join-irreducible coordinate calculations (Catalan counts 1,2,5,14,42,132,429,1430; diameters 0,1,4,7,12,17,24,31). Finite checks are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact graph diameter answers a natural shortest-swap question on Catalan-number permutation classes. The parity difference arises from uniqueness of maximal inversion rank and disjoint simple inversion atoms, not an arbitrary finite slice; the forbidden-pattern constraint creates a linearly growing detour relative to the full permutohedron. The proof identifies sharp witnesses uniformly for every size.
